prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 华东区门店2024年1—5月销量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "门店" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 92px
  col 2: header "1月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "2月" · longest unbreakable word 34px · one-line width 34px
  col 4: header "3月" · longest unbreakable word 34px · one-line width 34px
  col 5: header "4月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 6: header "5月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare monthly sales across East China stores and reveal each store's month-to-month trend over January–May.","reading":"Readers scan row by row to identify a store, then read left to right across the five months; they also compare a single month vertically across stores. The row-label column anchors each row, while the month columns form one continuous comparable series.","groups":["Column 1 (门店): row-label column identifying each store.","Columns 2–6 (1月–5月): one comparable time series; keep near-equal widths and consistent alignment so month-to-month differences read cleanly."],"keep_intact":["Month headers 1月–5月, unbroken.","All numeric sales values, with no wrapping, truncation, or overflow.","门店 header and the full characters of every store name; store names may wrap but must not be truncated."],"may_wrap":["Store names such as 上海徐汇店 and 南京新街口店 may wrap at Chinese character boundaries; row height can absorb two lines.","Month headers and numbers should not wrap."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [74, 57, 57, 57, 57, 57] · table 360×394px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [69, 58, 58, 58, 58, 58] · table 360×394px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [79, 56, 56, 56, 56, 56] · table 360×394px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"The five month columns are equal at 57px, so every 4-digit value has 36px of content space and sits comfortably on one line; headers stay unwrapped and vertical comparison across stores is clean.","problems":"门店 is the tightest element: its 53px text box makes the first line of every store name nearly touch the cell edge, so the row labels look squeezed against the numbers. The 1px surplus in each month column buys nothing because 35px already fits the values. The table reads as a numeric grid with a cramped label strip rather than rows anchored by readable labels.","cause":"col1=74 leaves only 53px for text, far below the 92px one-line need. Meanwhile each month column has 37px content, 2px more than needed, so the numeric area is loose while the labels are cramped. The eye notices the tight label column first.","cause":"col1=69 yields 48px text; months=58 yield 37px content. Each month has exactly 35px content for the 4-digit values, the label column has breathing room, and the table reads row-first as intended.","problems":"Store names still wrap to two lines; 5-character names break 3+2 such as 上海徐 / 汇店, leaving a short second line, and 6-character names break 3+3. The 60px row height and airy numeric cells follow from the mandatory two-line labels, not from a width error.","cause":"col1=79 gives 58px text, just under the 60px needed for 4 characters; months=56 give 35px content, exactly the longest number. This is the Pareto optimum under the 359px cap with equal month columns."}],"done":true,"designs":[]}
